{"type":"assistant","message":{"model":"claude-sonnet-5-5","id":"msg_011CgMmbjQA8M6eNeMijq2WW","type":"message","role":"assistant","content":[{"type":"text","text":"=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Regions.md ===\n# FEATURE: Regions\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The regions report counts events and the maximum magnitude per region of a saved feed. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MinMagFilter.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes regions |\n| Consumes    | filter_min_mag(events, m), region_of |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>` answers which regions are most active. It reads the file,\napplies the magnitude filter, groups events by region, and writes one CSV row per region.\n\n## Trigger\n\nThe command line `quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>`.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Read the file and drop events with a null magnitude (reader).\n2. Keep events with `mag >= m` when `--min-mag` is given (filter).\n3. Compute one row per region: event count and maximum magnitude (compute).\n4. Format and write CSV with the `csv` module, `\\n` line endings, UTF-8 (formatter).\n\n## Output\n\nHeader `region,events,max_mag`. Rows are ordered by `events` descending, then `region` ascending.\nRegion text is compared by byte value (its UTF-8 encoding). `max_mag` is written with one decimal\nplace. The region of an event is the text after the last `, ` in its place, or the whole place when\nthere is none; a null place is `Unknown`, which is its own region. With no matching events only the\nheader is written and the exit status is 0.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line. Nothing else.\n\n## Writes\n\nCSV on standard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC regions-counts-and-order ===\nIntent: Regions are grouped, counted and ordered by events descending then region bytes ascending.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place, t):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": t, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [10.0, 5.0, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\n# (place, region, mag)\nspecs = [\n    (\"5 km N of Town, Beta\", \"Beta\", 5.0),\n    (\"6 km N of Town, Beta\", \"Beta\", 6.2),\n    (\"7 km N of Town, Alpha\", \"Alpha\", 5.5),\n    (\"8 km N of Town, Alpha\", \"Alpha\", 5.1),\n    (\"9 km N of Town, Gamma\", \"Gamma\", 7.0),\n    (\"1 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.3),\n    (\"2 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.4),\n    (\"3 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.0),\n    (\"Plain Region Name\", \"Plain Region Name\", 5.6),\n    (\"4 km N of Town, Sub, Outer\", \"Outer\", 5.2),\n    (None, \"Unknown\", 5.7),\n]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p, BASE + i * 60000) for i, (p, r, m) in enumerate(specs)]\nfeatures.append(feat(99, None, \"1 km N of Town, Nullland\", BASE))\n\ncounts = {}\nmaxes = {}\nfor p, r, m in specs:\n    counts[r] = counts.get(r, 0) + 1\n    maxes[r] = max(maxes.get(r, m), m)\nexpected = sorted(counts, key=lambda r: (-counts[r], r.encode(\"utf-8\")))\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]\nbody = rows[1:]\nassert [r[0] for r in body] == expected\nfor r in body:\n    assert int(r[1]) == counts[r[0]]\n    assert float(r[2]) == maxes[r[0]]\nassert \"Nullland\" not in [r[0] for r in body]\n=== END AC regions-counts-and-order ===\n\n=== AC regions-min-mag-and-empty ===\nIntent: --min-mag restricts the regions report and an empty result is only the header with exit 0.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": BASE + i * 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [10.0, 5.0, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\nthreshold = 6.0\nspecs = [(\"1 km N of T, Low\", 5.0), (\"2 km N of T, Low\", 5.9),\n         (\"3 km N of T, High\", 6.0), (\"4 km N of T, High\", 6.8)]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p) for i, (p, m) in enumerate(specs)]\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", str(threshold), path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    kept = [m for p, m in specs if m >= threshold]\n    assert len(rows) == 2\n    assert rows[1][0] == \"High\"\n    assert int(rows[1][1]) == len(kept)\n    assert float(rows[1][2]) == max(kept)\n\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", \"99\", path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    assert rows == [[\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]]\n=== END AC regions-min-mag-and-empty ===\n\n=== AC regions-failure-contract ===\nIntent: A missing file exits 1 and an extra file argument exits 2, both with empty standard output.\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    missing = os.path.join(tmp, \"absent.geojson\")\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", missing)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", missing, missing)\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n=== END AC regions-failure-contract ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Region text is compared by byte value, never by locale collation.\n- No report value is embedded in code; every row is computed from the file being read.\n- A failing command writes nothing to standard output.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Near.md ===\n# FEATURE: Near\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The near report lists events within a haversine distance of a point, nearest first. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MinMagFilter.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes near, haversine_km |\n| Consumes    | filter_min_mag(events, m), format_time |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes near --lat <deg> --lon <deg> --radius <km> [--min-mag <m>] <file>` lists the events whose\ngreat-circle distance from the given point is at most the radius.\n\n## Trigger\n\nThe command line `quakes near ...` with all of `--lat`, `--lon` and `--radius`.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Read the file and drop events with a null magnitude.\n2. Apply `--min-mag` when given.\n3. Compute each event's haversine distance from (`--lat`, `--lon`) with `haversine_km`.\n4. Keep events whose unrounded distance is `<= --radius` (decision Q-003).\n5. Order by unrounded distance ascending, then time ascending.\n6. Write CSV; distance is rounded half up to one decimal place.\n\n## Distance\n\nHaversine on a sphere of radius 6371.0 km, angles in radians:\n\n```text\nh = sin^2((lat2 - lat1) / 2) + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin^2((lon2 - lon1) / 2)\nd = 2 * 6371.0 * asin(sqrt(h))\n```\n\n`haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) -> float` is a pure function in the compute module.\n\n## Output\n\nHeader `distance_km,time,mag,place,id`. Time is UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; magnitude has one decimal\nplace. Places containing commas are quoted by the `csv` module. With no matching events only the\nheader is written and the exit status is 0.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line.\n\n## Writes\n\nCSV on standard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC near-order-and-distance ===\nIntent: Events within the radius are listed nearest first with ties broken by time and one-decimal distances.\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport re\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dp = p2 - p1\n    dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place, t, lon, lat):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": t, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\n# (id suffix, mag, place, time, lon, lat); center is (0, 0)\nevents = [\n    (0, 5.5, \"far, Faraway\", BASE + 1000, 3.0, 0.0),\n    (1, 5.1, \"late one, Nearby\", BASE + 9000, 1.0, 0.0),\n    (2, 5.2, \"mid, Midway\", BASE + 5000, 2.0, 0.0),\n    (3, 5.3, \"early one, Nearby\", BASE + 2000, 1.0, 0.0),\n]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p, t, lo, la) for (i, m, p, t, lo, la) in events]\nradius = 250.0\nlat0, lon0 = 0.0, 0.0\n\ninside = [e for e in events if hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4]) <= radius]\ninside.sort(key=lambda e: (hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4]), e[3]))\nassert 0 < len(inside) < len(events)\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", str(lat0), \"--lon\", str(lon0),\n                                \"--radius\", str(radius), path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"distance_km\", \"time\", \"mag\", \"place\", \"id\"]\nbody = rows[1:]\nassert [r[4] for r in body] == [\"ev%d\" % e[0] for e in inside]\nfor r, e in zip(body, inside):\n    d = hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4])\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d\", r[0])\n    assert abs(float(r[0]) - d) <= 0.0501\n    stamp = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(e[3] / 1000, datetime.timezone.utc)\n    assert r[1] == stamp.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\")\n    assert float(r[2]) == e[1]\n    assert r[3] == e[2]\n=== END AC near-order-and-distance ===\n\n=== AC near-radius-uses-unrounded-distance ===\nIntent: The radius comparison uses the unrounded distance, so a radius just below it excludes the event and one just above includes it.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes fetch --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --end <YYYY-MM-DD> [--min-mag <m>] --out <file>` saves a period\nof the USGS FDSN event feed so that report commands can read it later.\n\n## Request\n\nGET `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query` with the query parameters `format=geojson`,\n`starttime=<start>`, `endtime=<end>`, `minmagnitude=<m>` An `HTTPError` is returned as its status code. No test uses the network.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Parse and validate options (`--start`, `--end`, `--out` required; `--min-mag` optional).\n2. Request the URL through `http_get`.\n3. On status 200, parse the body as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (failure handling is in\n   FEATURE-FetchErrors.md).\n4. Write the body bytes unchanged to `--out`.\n5. Write `fetched,<count>` to standard output, where `<count>` is the number of features.\n\nMissing `--start`, `--end` or `--out`, an extra positional argument, or a malformed `--min-mag` is a\nusage error (exit 2).\n\n## Reads\n\nThe USGS event service.\n\n## Writes\n\nThe file named by `--out`; `fetched,<count>` on standard output.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC fetch-request-and-save ===\nIntent: Fetch requests the FDSN query with the given range and default magnitude, saves the body unchanged and reports the feature count.\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nimport \"time\": 1735689600000 + i,\n                                               \"tsunami\": 0},\n             \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 2.0, 3.0]}, \"id\": \"id%d\" % i}\n            for i in range(3)]\nbody = json.dumps({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, indent=3).encode(\"utf-8\") + b\"\\n\"\nseen = []\n\ndef fake_urlopen(req, *a, **kw):\n mock.patch(\"urllib.request.urlopen\", fake_urlopen):\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"fetch\", \"--start\", start, \"--end\", end, \"--out\", out_path)\n    print(out)\n    print(err)\n    assert code == 0\n    with open(out_path, \"rb\") as fh:\n        assert fh.read() == body\n    fields = out.strip().split(\",\")\n    assert fields[0] == \"fetched\"\n    assert int(fields[1]) == BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Regions.md ===\n# FEATURE: Regions\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The regions report counts events and the maximum magnitude per region of a saved feed. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MinMagFilter.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes regions |\n| Consumes    | filter_min_mag(events, m), region_of |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>` answers which regions are most active. It reads the file,\napplies the magnitude filter, groups events by region, and writes one CSV row per region.\n\n## Trigger\n\nThe command line `quakes regions [--min-mag <m>] <file>`.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Read the file and drop events with a null magnitude (reader).\n2. Keep events with `mag >= m` when `--min-mag` is given (filter).\n3. Compute one row per region: event count and maximum magnitude (compute).\n4. Format and write CSV with the `csv` module, `\\n` line endings, UTF-8 (formatter).\n\n## Output\n\nHeader `region,events,max_mag`. Rows are ordered by `events` descending, then `region` ascending.\nRegion text is compared by byte value (its UTF-8 encoding). `max_mag` is written with one decimal\nplace. The region of an event is the text after the last `, ` in its place, or the whole place when\nthere is none; a null place is `Unknown`, which is its own region. With no matching events only the\nheader is written and the exit status is 0.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line. Nothing else.\n\n## Writes\n\nCSV on standard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC regions-counts-and-order ===\nIntent: Regions are grouped, counted and ordered by events descending then region bytes ascending.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place, t):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": t, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [10.0, 5.0, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\n# (place, region, mag)\nspecs = [\n    (\"5 km N of Town, Beta\", \"Beta\", 5.0),\n    (\"6 km N of Town, Beta\", \"Beta\", 6.2),\n    (\"7 km N of Town, Alpha\", \"Alpha\", 5.5),\n    (\"8 km N of Town, Alpha\", \"Alpha\", 5.1),\n    (\"9 km N of Town, Gamma\", \"Gamma\", 7.0),\n    (\"1 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.3),\n    (\"2 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.4),\n    (\"3 km N of Town, alpha\", \"alpha\", 5.0),\n    (\"Plain Region Name\", \"Plain Region Name\", 5.6),\n    (\"4 km N of Town, Sub, Outer\", \"Outer\", 5.2),\n    (None, \"Unknown\", 5.7),\n]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p, BASE + i * 60000) for i, (p, r, m) in enumerate(specs)]\nfeatures.append(feat(99, None, \"1 km N of Town, Nullland\", BASE))\n\ncounts = {}\nmaxes = {}\nfor p, r, m in specs:\n    counts[r] = counts.get(r, 0) + 1\n    maxes[r] = max(maxes.get(r, m), m)\nexpected = sorted(counts, key=lambda r: (-counts[r], r.encode(\"utf-8\")))\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]\nbody = rows[1:]\nassert [r[0] for r in body] == expected\nfor r in body:\n    assert int(r[1]) == counts[r[0]]\n    assert float(r[2]) == maxes[r[0]]\nassert \"Nullland\" not in [r[0] for r in body]\n=== END AC regions-counts-and-order ===\n\n=== AC regions-min-mag-and-empty ===\nIntent: --min-mag restricts the regions report and an empty result is only the header with exit 0.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": BASE + i * 1000, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [10.0, 5.0, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\nthreshold = 6.0\nspecs = [(\"1 km N of T, Low\", 5.0), (\"2 km N of T, Low\", 5.9),\n         (\"3 km N of T, High\", 6.0), (\"4 km N of T, High\", 6.8)]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p) for i, (p, m) in enumerate(specs)]\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", str(threshold), path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    kept = [m for p, m in specs if m >= threshold]\n    assert len(rows) == 2\n    assert rows[1][0] == \"High\"\n    assert int(rows[1][1]) == len(kept)\n    assert float(rows[1][2]) == max(kept)\n\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", \"--min-mag\", \"99\", path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    assert rows == [[\"region\", \"events\", \"max_mag\"]]\n=== END AC regions-min-mag-and-empty ===\n\n=== AC regions-failure-contract ===\nIntent: A missing file exits 1 and an extra file argument exits 2, both with empty standard output.\n\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    missing = os.path.join(tmp, \"absent.geojson\")\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", missing)\n    assert code == 1\n    assert out == \"\"\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"regions\", missing, missing)\n    assert code == 2\n    assert out == \"\"\n=== END AC regions-failure-contract ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Region text is compared by byte value, never by locale collation.\n- No report value is embedded in code; every row is computed from the file being read.\n- A failing command writes nothing to standard output.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Near.md ===\n# FEATURE: Near\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The near report lists events within a haversine distance of a point, nearest first. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-MinMagFilter.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md |\n| Provides    | quakes near, haversine_km |\n| Consumes    | filter_min_mag(events, m), format_time |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes near --lat <deg> --lon <deg> --radius <km> [--min-mag <m>] <file>` lists the events whose\ngreat-circle distance from the given point is at most the radius.\n\n## Trigger\n\nThe command line `quakes near ...` with all of `--lat`, `--lon` and `--radius`.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Read the file and drop events with a null magnitude.\n2. Apply `--min-mag` when given.\n3. Compute each event's haversine distance from (`--lat`, `--lon`) with `haversine_km`.\n4. Keep events whose unrounded distance is `<= --radius` (decision Q-003).\n5. Order by unrounded distance ascending, then time ascending.\n6. Write CSV; distance is rounded half up to one decimal place.\n\n## Distance\n\nHaversine on a sphere of radius 6371.0 km, angles in radians:\n\n```text\nh = sin^2((lat2 - lat1) / 2) + cos(lat1) * cos(lat2) * sin^2((lon2 - lon1) / 2)\nd = 2 * 6371.0 * asin(sqrt(h))\n```\n\n`haversine_km(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2) -> float` is a pure function in the compute module.\n\n## Output\n\nHeader `distance_km,time,mag,place,id`. Time is UTC `YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ`; magnitude has one decimal\nplace. Places containing commas are quoted by the `csv` module. With no matching events only the\nheader is written and the exit status is 0.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe saved GeoJSON file named on the command line.\n\n## Writes\n\nCSV on standard output only.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC near-order-and-distance ===\nIntent: Events within the radius are listed nearest first with ties broken by time and one-decimal distances.\n\nimport csv\nimport datetime\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport re\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dp = p2 - p1\n    dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin(dp / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))\n\ndef feat(i, mag, place, t, lon, lat):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": place, \"time\": t, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, lat, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\n# (id suffix, mag, place, time, lon, lat); center is (0, 0)\nevents = [\n    (0, 5.5, \"far, Faraway\", BASE + 1000, 3.0, 0.0),\n    (1, 5.1, \"late one, Nearby\", BASE + 9000, 1.0, 0.0),\n    (2, 5.2, \"mid, Midway\", BASE + 5000, 2.0, 0.0),\n    (3, 5.3, \"early one, Nearby\", BASE + 2000, 1.0, 0.0),\n]\nfeatures = [feat(i, m, p, t, lo, la) for (i, m, p, t, lo, la) in events]\nradius = 250.0\nlat0, lon0 = 0.0, 0.0\n\ninside = [e for e in events if hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4]) <= radius]\ninside.sort(key=lambda e: (hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4]), e[3]))\nassert 0 < len(inside) < len(events)\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": features}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", str(lat0), \"--lon\", str(lon0),\n                                \"--radius\", str(radius), path)\nprint(out)\nprint(err)\nassert code == 0\nrows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\nassert rows[0] == [\"distance_km\", \"time\", \"mag\", \"place\", \"id\"]\nbody = rows[1:]\nassert [r[4] for r in body] == [\"ev%d\" % e[0] for e in inside]\nfor r, e in zip(body, inside):\n    d = hav(lat0, lon0, e[5], e[4])\n    assert re.fullmatch(r\"\\d+\\.\\d\", r[0])\n    assert abs(float(r[0]) - d) <= 0.0501\n    stamp = datetime.datetime.fromtimestamp(e[3] / 1000, datetime.timezone.utc)\n    assert r[1] == stamp.strftime(\"%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ\")\n    assert float(r[2]) == e[1]\n    assert r[3] == e[2]\n=== END AC near-order-and-distance ===\n\n=== AC near-radius-uses-unrounded-distance ===\nIntent: The radius comparison uses the unrounded distance, so a radius just below it excludes the event and one just above includes it.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport math\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef hav(lat1, lon1, lat2, lon2):\n    p1, p2 = math.radians(lat1), math.radians(lat2)\n    dl = math.radians(lon2 - lon1)\n    h = math.sin((p2 - p1) / 2) ** 2 + math.cos(p1) * math.cos(p2) * math.sin(dl / 2) ** 2\n    return 2 * 6371.0 * math.asin(math.sqrt(h))\n\nevent = {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n         \"properties\": {\"mag\": 5.0, \"place\": \"x, Region\", \"time\": BASE, \"tsunami\": 0},\n         \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [1.0, 0.0, 10]},\n         \"id\": \"only\"}\nd = hav(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 1.0)\nbelow = math.floor(d * 10) / 10\nabove = math.ceil(d * 10) / 10\nassert below < d < above\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [event]}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"%.1f\" % below, path)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert len(list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))) == 1\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"%.1f\" % above, path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    assert len(rows) == 2\n    assert rows[1][4] == \"only\"\n=== END AC near-radius-uses-unrounded-distance ===\n\n=== AC near-min-mag-and-empty ===\nIntent: --min-mag applies to near and a search with no matches writes only the header with exit 0.\n\nimport csv\nimport io\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nBASE = 1735689600000\n\ndef feat(i, mag, lon):\n    return {\"type\": \"Feature\",\n            \"properties\": {\"mag\": mag, \"place\": \"p%d, Region\" % i, \"time\": BASE + i, \"tsunami\": 0},\n            \"geometry\": {\"type\": \"Point\", \"coordinates\": [lon, 0.0, 10]},\n            \"id\": \"ev%d\" % i}\n\nspecs = [(0, 5.0, 0.5), (1, 6.5, 0.6), (2, 5.5, 0.7)]\nthreshold = 5.5\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": [feat(*s) for s in specs]}, fh)\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"500\",\n                                \"--min-mag\", str(threshold), path)\n    print(out)\n    assert code == 0\n    rows = list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out)))\n    kept = sorted(\"ev%d\" % i for i, m, lo in specs if m >= threshold)\n    assert sorted(r[4] for r in rows[1:]) == kept\n\n    code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", \"--lat\", \"60\", \"--lon\", \"100\", \"--radius\", \"10\", path)\n    assert code == 0\n    assert list(csv.reader(io.StringIO(out))) == [[\"distance_km\", \"time\", \"mag\", \"place\", \"id\"]]\n=== END AC near-min-mag-and-empty ===\n\n=== AC near-haversine-function ===\nIntent: haversine_km is a pure function that returns zero for identical points and a symmetric positive distance otherwise.\n\nimport importlib\nimport pkgutil\nimport cli\n\nfound = None\nfor mod in pkgutil.walk_packages(cli.__path__, \"cli.\"):\n    if mod.name.endswith(\".testing\"):\n        continue\n    m = importlib.import_module(mod.name)\n    if hasattr(m, \"haversine_km\"):\n        found = m.haversine_km\n        break\nassert found is not None\nassert found(10.0, 20.0, 10.0, 20.0) == 0\na = found(0.0, 0.0, 0.0, 90.0)\nb = found(0.0, 90.0, 0.0, 0.0)\nassert a > 0\nassert abs(a - b) < 1e-9\n=== END AC near-haversine-function ===\n\n## User Acceptance\n\n- None.\n\n## Guardrails\n\n- Distance uses a sphere of radius 6371.0 km; no other earth model.\n- The radius comparison uses the unrounded distance; rounding is for display only.\n- No distance is embedded in code; every value is computed from the file being read.\n- A failing command writes nothing to standard output.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-NearValidation.md ===\n# FEATURE: Near Validation\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The near command rejects out-of-range or missing coordinates and radius as usage errors. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-Near.md |\n| Provides    | near option validation |\n| Consumes    | quakes near |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\nGuarantee that `quakes near` only runs with a valid point and radius, and otherwise fails as a usage\nerror before reading the file.\n\n## Rules\n\n- `--lat` must be within -90 to 90 inclusive.\n- `--lon` must be within -180 to 180 inclusive.\n- `--radius` must be greater than zero.\n- All three of `--lat`, `--lon` and `--radius` are required.\n- Any violation exits 2, writes nothing to standard output, and writes one diagnostic line to\n  standard error.\n- The boundary values -90, 90, -180 and 180 are valid.\n\n## Reads\n\nThe command line only.\n\n## Writes\n\nNothing on standard output on failure; one line on standard error.\n\n## Programmatic Acceptance\n\n=== AC near-validation-rejects ===\nIntent: Out-of-range or missing near options exit 2 with empty standard output and one diagnostic line.\n\nimport json\nimport os\nimport tempfile\nfrom cli.testing import cli_runner\n\nwith tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:\n    path = os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}, fh)\n    cases = [\n        [\"--lat\", \"95\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"-90.5\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"180.5\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"-181\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"0\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"-5\"],\n        [\"--lon\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"0\", \"--lon\", \"0\"],\n        [],\n    ]\n    for opts in cases:\n        code, out, err = cli_runner(\"near\", *opts, path)\n        print(opts, code, repr(err))\n        assert code == 2\n        assert out == \"\"\n        assert len(err.strip().splitlines()) == 1\n=== END AC near-validation-rejects ===\n\n=== AC near-validation-accepts-boundaries ===\nIntent: The inclusive boundary values for latitude and longitude and a os.path.join(tmp, \"q.geojson\")\n    with open(path, \"w\", encoding=\"utf-8\") as fh:\n        json.dump({\"type\": \"FeatureCollection\", \"features\": []}, fh)\n    cases = [\n        [\"--lat\", \"90\", \"--lon\", \"180\", \"--radius\", \"10\"],\n        [\"--lat\", \"-90\", \"--lon\", \"-180\", \"--radius\", \"0.5\"],\n    ]\n    for opts in cases:\n        code, out, err = Guardrails\n\n- Validation failures never write to standard output.\n- Messages are diagnostics only and are never part of the contract.\n=== END ARTIFACT ===\n=== BEGIN ARTIFACT FEATURE-Fetch.md ===\n# FEATURE: Fetch\n\n| Field       | Value |\n|-------------|-------|\n| Version     | 20261024 V1 |\n| Description | The fetch command downloads a period of the USGS event feed as GeoJSON and saves the body unchanged. |\n| Depends On  | FEATURE-CliDispatch.md, FEATURE-ExitCodes.md, FEATURE-FeedReader.md |\n| Provides    | quakes fetch, http_get |\n| Consumes    | quakes <command> dispatch |\n\n## Questions\n\n- None.\n\n## Purpose\n\n`quakes fetch --start <YYYY-MM-DD> --end <YYYY-MM-DD> [--min-mag <m>] --out <file>` saves a period\nof the USGS FDSN event feed so that report commands can read it later.\n\n## Request\n\nGET `https://earthquake.usgs.gov/fdsnws/event/1/query` with the query parameters `format=geojson`,\n`starttime=<start>`, `endtime=<end>`, `minmagnitude=<m>` (default `2.5`) and `orderby=time-asc`.\n\n## HTTP seam\n\nAll network access goes through one replaceable function, `http_get(url)`, which returns the status\ncode and the body bytes. It calls `urllib.request.urlopen` through the module attribute\n(`urllib.request.urlopen(...)`, never `from urllib.request import urlopen`), so a test can replace\nthe HTTP call with a stub. An `HTTPError` is returned as its status code. No test uses the network.\n\n## Sequence\n\n1. Parse and validate options (`--start`, `--end`, `--out` required; `--min-mag` optional).\n2. Request the URL through `http_get`.\n3. On status 200, parse the body as a GeoJSON FeatureCollection (failure handling is in\n   FEATURE-FetchErrors.md).\n4. Write the body bytes unchanged to `--out`.\n5. Write `fetched,<count>` to standard output, where `<count>` is the number of features.\n\nMissing `--start`, `--end` or `--out`, an extra positional argument, or a malformed `--min-mag` is a\nusage
